properties.name: Through a hub, every tool runs on one named member, and every id in a routed reply carries its prefix
properties.rationale: P4a of phase 4 (Anthony 2026-10-19, "proceed to phase 4"), requirement reflow2:req:through-a-hub-every-tool-can-run-on-one-named-member. It was measured in the Arrow, cogito and trolley trials: through the hub, a tool with no node id could not be pointed at the member under study; a search could not be kept to one member, which put the observer's own records in front of a blind designer; and the one-PR hold had to be released through the chat connector. The door is one argument rather than per-tool design lists. dec:how-a-session-opens-a-view-over-several-designs rejected (d), 197 schema changes and a choice on every call. `member` is optional, generated in one place, and declared only where a view is served (a hub's listing). So a design served alone, and every local server, publishes byte for byte what it did, and the toolsnaps do not move. Routing by an id's prefix now runs before the not-viewed list. Before this, fact:a-release-tool-through-a-hub-writes-a-member-prefixed-id-into-the-hub-2026-10-19 was observed: add_release stored "reflow2:rel:v0880" in the hub. No cause is recorded for that fact here; it was not walked with the root-cause skill. The id prefix moved from a key-named rule to a rule that also reads values: a string anywhere in the reply that the member holds as a node id, or that the call passed with the prefix, gets the prefix. So a new reply field cannot slip back to bare ids the way assumes and conclusion did. Prose in a successful reply is left alone, because it may be stored content, and a prefix pasted back inside prose would be stored with it. Live evidence while recording this change, on flo2.io 0.88.0 through the hub: add_capability's near-match refusal and its distinct_from echo, and add_verification's `verifies` echo, all came back bare. Tests first: 5 of 5 failed on main 4bcfddafb. Host contract: flo2 must send reflow2/view_graph_ids on a hub's tools/list as it does on calls; a flo2 counterpart is owed. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Through a hub's address, any call may pass `member` (a member's graph_id, or the hub's), and the tool runs on that design alone. This covers the tools that take no node id and the ones the view does not otherwise serve, and keeps search_design and scan_nodes to one design. A hub's tools/list declares `member` on every tool when the listing names the view, and no other listing changes. An id's '<member>:' prefix now routes every tool, the not-viewed ones included, so add_release no longer stores a member-prefixed id in the hub. Every id a member's reply holds now comes back prefixed: by key, by value (an id the call passed or a node the member holds), and in a refusal's words.
